title: Error burst correlation pane and adaptive sampling for trace enrichment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an interactive error burst correlation pane in the Console that links metric spikes to enriched traces using adaptive sampling. Purpose is to make short-lived, high-severity bursts (timeouts, overload queues, model rejections, 5xx/gRPC errors) immediately actionable without overwhelming trace storage or noise budgets.

Problem statement: We routinely see short bursts of failed inference requests that are hard to diagnose because sampling is uniform and metrics and traces are siloed. Examples: a 3-minute window of model rejections concurrent with VGPU queue growth and elevated 5xx responses, followed by a drop once autoscaling kicks in. Current dashboards surface the metric spikes but operators must manually increase trace sampling, clobbering budget and still missing the exact correlation.

Goals:
- Surface a single-pane view that correlates metric spikes across request latency, queue depth, model_reject_rate, http_5xx_rate, and grpc_status_codes.
- Compute a burst_index score that weights co-occurrence and slope change to rank incidents.
- Trigger adaptive trace sampling and a short-duration full-context capture when burst_index crosses thresholds.
- Enrich captured traces with model_metadata (model_name, model_version, quantization), route metadata, region, instance_type, and recent deploy tag.
- Provide a quick link from the pane to a curated incident timeline and suggested next actions.

Design and telemetry:
- Derived metric: burst_index = 0.5 * normalized(latency_delta) + 0.3 * normalized(queue_delta) + 0.2 * normalized(error_rate_delta). We will compute using the metrics pipeline with a 1m and 5m rolling window.
- Metrics used: request_latency_p50_p95_p99, kube_gpu_queue_depth, model_reject_rate, http_5xx_rate, grpc_non_ok_rate, inflight_requests.
- Adaptive sampling: when burst_index > 0.7 for a route or org, increase trace sampling factor to 100% for 5 minutes and capture top 200 traces by latency and error. Sampling controller implemented as a lightweight service connected to tracehooks.
- Trace enrichment: runtime must add model_version, batch_size, token_count, route_id, and applied_policy into trace attributes. Log pipeline will upsert these into trace payloads using trace_id as join key.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pane displays correlated time series and a ranked list of active bursts with burst_index and affected routes.
2) Clicking a burst toggles an incident timeline with sample traces and linked PRs/deploys in the last 30 minutes.
3) Adaptive sampling reliably triggers and captures full context traces within 30s of threshold crossing.
4) Storage and cost impact stays within the allocated observability budget in staged environments.
5) Oncall can create a follow-up ticket from pane with prepopulated tags for postmortem.

Implementation tasks:
- Metrics: add burst_index calculation to metrics pipeline (ENG). Query prototype in PromQL:
  burst_index(route) = 0.5 * ((p95_latency_1m - p95_latency_5m)/p95_latency_5m) + 0.3 * ((queue_1m - queue_5m)/max(queue_5m,1)) + 0.2 * ((error_rate_1m - error_rate_5m)/max(error_rate_5m,0.001))
- Tracing: extend tracehooks API to accept sampling directives from controller and to attach model metadata. Patch runtime to emit metadata tags.
- Log pipeline: enrich traces by joining recent log entries keyed on trace_id; add processor in log-forwarder.
- Console UI: new pane in alerting/insights product area, implement charting and ranked list, incident detail drawer, and export to ticket.
- Ops: quota and budget controls for staging and prod, fallback to rate-limited behavior if storage budget exceeded.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: internal staging environment, burst_index visible, adaptive sampling disabled for validation. (2 weeks)
- Stage 2: enable adaptive sampling for internal customers only, monitor cost and capture quality, iterate. (2 weeks)
- Stage 3: opt-in alpha for select customers with an experimental toggle, gather feedback and adjust thresholds. (3 weeks)
- Stage 4: general availability with guardrails and SLOs on observability budget.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: adaptive sampling could spike trace storage cost. Mitigation: hard cap per-org daily trace increases and early abort when ingestion rate grows beyond threshold.
- Risk: runtime changes could add latency. Mitigation: emit metadata asynchronously and benchmark; default to best-effort enrichment.
- Risk: burst_index false positives. Mitigation: tune weights and require cross-signal confirmation before triggering 100% sampling.

Monitoring and success metrics:
- Reduce mean time to root cause for burst incidents by 40% in staging tests.
- 90th percentile time from burst detection to full-context trace available under 60s.
- Observability cost delta less than 12% for alpha orgs compared to baseline.
